questions.knowledge_point: Solving Second-Order IVPs When the Characteristic Equation Has Imaginary Roots
questions.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{y}^{″}+16y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=A\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+B\operatorname{cos}⁡4x,
$$

solve the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{″}+16y=0,\,y(0)=1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=-4.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We find the constants $A$ and $B$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(0)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=-4,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=4A\operatorname{cos}⁡4x-4B\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=-4$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4=4A\,⟹\,A=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=-\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\operatorname{cos}⁡4x.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving Second-Order IVPs When the Characteristic Equation Has Repeated Roots
questions.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y=A{e}^{-x}+Bx{e}^{-x},
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+y=0,\,y(0)=8,\,{y}^{′}(0)=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We find the constants $A$ and $B$ using the initial conditions. 

- Substituting $y(0)=8$ into the general solution gives

$$
A=8.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=0,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-A{e}^{-x}+B{e}^{-x}-Bx{e}^{-x}.
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=0$ into the above gives

$$
-A+B=0.
$$

Using the fact that $A=8$ gives $B=8.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=8{e}^{-x}+8x{e}^{-x}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving Second-Order IVPs When the Characteristic Equation Has Complex Roots
questions.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+17y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡4x),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+17y=0,\,y(0)=-1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=-11.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions. 

- Substituting $y(0)=-1$ into the general solution gives

$$
P=-1.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=-11,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-{e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡4x)+{e}^{-x}(-4P\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+4Q\operatorname{cos}⁡4x).
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(0)=-11$ into the above to get

$$
-P+4Q=-11.
$$

Using the fact that $P=-1$ gives $Q=-3.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{-x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡4x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡4x).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving Second-Order IVPs When the Characteristic Equation Has Complex Roots
questions.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+2y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+2y=0,\,y(0)=2,\,{y}^{′}(0)=-2.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions. 

- Substituting $y(0)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
P=2.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=-2,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-{e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+{e}^{-x}(-P\operatorname{sin}⁡x+Q\operatorname{cos}⁡x).
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(0)=-2$ into the above to get

$$
-P+Q=-2.
$$

Using the fact that $P=2$ gives $Q=0.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
